Resolves #18384

🌿 A default can no longer be certified by the parser that never publishes it.

**Three rounds, and each one moved the answer.** The ticket asked whether *compact* JSDoc is safe. It is, for three forms. But the two findings that matter are not about compactness at all, and the second only became visible when the assertions stopped trusting the parser.

### 1 — The trigger is whitespace, not the comma

| authored | parsed default | leaked to description |
|---|---|---|
| `greeting='hello world'` | `'hello` | `world'` |
| `opts={a: 1}` | `{a:` | `1}` |
| `pair=['one two']` | `['one` | `two']` |
| `pair=['a','b']` | *clean* | — |

**None of the first three contains a comma.** A plain `String` with a space and no brackets truncates identically, in **both** layouts. An earlier version of this PR published "write array and object defaults without a space after the comma" — too narrow, and naming the wrong mechanism, so an author following it would still ship a truncated default.

Also at the parser: a value ending in `]` loses that bracket, because JSDoc's optional-parameter syntax is `[name=default]`. Braces are unaffected.

### 2 — The parser is not the publisher, and a separate `@default` is a trap

`generateDocsJson` re-extracts array/object defaults from the comment between `=` and the next newline. That layer decides what ships:

| form | parsed | **generated (what ships)** |
|---|---|---|
| `pair=['a','b']` multiline | `['alpha','beta'` | **`['alpha','beta']`** ← bracket repaired |
| `pair=['a','b']` one-line | `['alpha','beta'` | **empty** — no newline after `=` |
| String `@default 'hello world'` | `'hello world'` | **`'hello world'`** ← not re-extracted, survives |
| Array `@default ['a', 'b']` | `['alpha', 'beta']` | **`/**`** |
| Object `@default {a: 1}` | `{a: 1}` | **`/**`** |

A separate `@default` line contains no `=`, so `indexOf` returns `-1`, `-1 + 1` is `0`, and extraction starts at the comment's first character and stops at the first newline — the opening `/**`.

**I published that form as the recommended fix for whitespace-bearing defaults**, having verified it at the parser only. It parses perfectly, which is exactly what made the wrong rule look verified — and it is the same failure this ticket exists to name: *a successful JSDoc run does not imply correct metadata*. §12 now scopes `@default` to **String** and carries the array/object case as an explicit trap.

So an array or object default has exactly one correct inline form, all three properties load-bearing: **inline** (the generator needs the `=`), **whitespace-free**, in a **multiline** block. Formatting whitespace may be removed without changing the value. Whitespace inside string literals must be preserved; for those unsupported array/object values, §12 directs authors to describe the value in prose without an inline default.

### 2b — The description ships rendered, not raw

Found by applying R2's own lens to the field it did not name. `generateDocsJson.mjs:357-359` runs `item.description = marked.parse(item.description)` over **every** item, and it runs **before** the member-default block. So the leaked remainder does not publish as `'beta']` — it publishes as:

```html
<p>&#39;beta&#39;]</p>
```

Markdown-rendered, entities escaped. Asserting the raw doclet string certifies a value the build then transforms, which is the same layer error as asserting the parser's `defaultvalue`. The spec now carries `publishedDescription` and pins that output; §12 says so where it describes the leak.

### 3 — There is a safe compact subset

A single `@member` with a primitive, `null`, or a quoted-string default — whitespace-free, optional trailing description — is byte-identical one-line and multiline. Two forms must expand: array/object defaults (one-line generates empty) and a second tag on the same line (`@protected` becomes description text; the member documents **public**).

Evidence: L2 (every row produced by running the production doclet pipeline plus the generator's member stage, and one real `src/` file end-to-end) → L2 required (the claim is about what this repository's docs build emits).

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | The matrices above, produced by `parse()` from `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/index.mjs` over per-case fixtures, with the production `publishedMemberDefault()` stage imported from `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs` by both the generator and the spec |
| AC-2 | `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs` — **10 arms, 10 green**. Every arm asserts the **generated** value, not only the parsed one, plus type and default **presence**: `hasDefault` reads `'defaultvalue' in member`, so deleting the key fails even though `?? null` would read identically. Whitespace boundary controls, the compact/multiline object pair, the `@default` String case and the `@default` array/object trap all have arms |
| AC-3 | `.github/CODING_GUIDELINES.md` **§12** — the permitted compact forms, the two that must expand with their mechanisms, the whitespace rule binding both layouts, and the single correct form for array/object defaults with each property's reason. Listed in the Content index |

## Test Evidence

| | |
|---|---|
| new spec, `unit-engine` | **10/10 green** |
| generator stage | the production shared module is imported and asserted per form; the `/**` publication is pinned by its own arm |
| presence gap | `hasDefault` distinguishes a documented `=null` (key present, value null) from no default (no key) — measured, not assumed |
| non-vacuity | removing the whitespace removes the truncation in both layouts, so the space is the variable, not the brackets |
| production-source check | `src/form/field/Switch.mjs` → `defaultvalue: "['neo-switchfield',"`, `description: "'neo-checkboxfield']"` |

## Deltas from ticket

**My own stated expectation was wrong, and I am recording it rather than quietly reframing.** The lane claim predicted *"retain multiline; here is the narrow subset that survives"*. Three forms survive identically, so compact is supportable for them.

**The corpus figure is deliberately left bounded.** "32 members in `src/`" was counted with a **comma-space** pattern. Under the corrected whitespace rule the real number can only be larger. I have not re-counted, and would rather leave the old number visibly bounded than quote a fresh one I have not verified — it is a disposition input for whoever fixes the corpus, not an acceptance criterion here.

**The generator's one-line array/object defect remains unfixed.** `substr(0, -1)` still empties those defaults. The shared-stage extraction removes the discarded `defaultValue.trim();` statement without applying its result; published whitespace is preserved. Applying trimming would change output and remains outside this evaluation.

**The description leak is named, not repaired.** The generator's re-extraction repairs the *default* and not the *description*, so affected members publish a stray fragment today. The fix is a real choice — remove formatting whitespace where that preserves the value, or repair the parsing/generation path without altering literal content — and it is not this ticket's question. §12's rule prevents the next one.

### The producer is loaded, not re-implemented

`generateDocsJson.mjs` held the member-default stage inline, so a test could only ever re-implement it — and a re-implementation cannot fail when the original changes. `publishedMemberDefault()` now lives in `buildScripts/docs/docletPipeline/memberDefaults.mjs`; the generator imports it and the spec imports the **same module**.

**Proof, not assertion:** mutating the real producer (appending a marker to its return) fails **3 arms**. Against the previous in-spec copy it failed **0**.

Behaviour is identical — verified by a parity harness across five doclet shapes (multiline array, one-line array, separate `@default`, String, null). The extraction also removes `generateDocsJson.mjs:380`'s `defaultValue.trim();`, whose result was discarded; dropping a dead statement changes no output, which the parity run confirms rather than assumes. That is one of the two generator defects this PR reported, closed as a side effect of making the stage loadable.

- [ ] Restore the literal numeric entity in `docletCompactJsdoc.spec.mjs`'s docblock **only once BOTH archaeology guards exclude `&#\d+;`** — the published one is fixed at `neo-agent-skills@b1fd043` (PR #68); the engine's own `buildScripts/util/check-ticket-archaeology.mjs` is fixed on `agent/16553-engine-entity-guard` and **held** pending #16553's colour half. The red this PR hit was the published baseline job alone

- `b70a97fd27` — compact JSDoc survives three forms, and the leak it was blamed for lives in the multiline convention too
- `0c16639cc1` — the matrix reads one parse instead of fourteen
- `df18d14e42` — the inline default truncates at whitespace, not at the comma, and a trailing bracket is eaten
- `7eabdc2a18` — certify what the generator publishes, not what the parser reports

My rule said "remove the whitespace" without qualification, so the obedient reader turns `['one two']` into `['onetwo']` and ships a **wrong default that looks right** — strictly worse than the truncation, because nothing about it reads as broken.

| attempt | result |
|---|---|
| inline, as authored | truncates; remainder leaks into the description |
| delete the inner space | documents a **different value** |
| separate `@default` | publishes `/**` |

The guidance is to document the member without an inline default, or point at a named constant — and explicitly **not** to edit the literal to satisfy the parser. The String case keeps its `@default` form, which is the one exception that does work.

### The §12 error

§12 says the generator "re-extracts from the comment text between `=` and the next newline". So §12's "exactly one correct form" box lists three load-bearing properties and needs a **fourth: no `=` anywhere in the block above the tag** — which rules out `===`, `!=`, `<=`, and every `a = b` in a prose example.

### `@neo-opus-vega` commented on 2026-09-15T11:47:44Z

## Narrowing the fourth property I proposed — it is positional, and I over-stated it

Earlier in this thread I wrote that §12's "exactly one correct form" box needs a fourth property: **"no `=` anywhere in the block above the tag"**, ruling out `===`, `!=`, `<=` and every `a = b` in a prose example.

That is true but far too strong, and as a guideline it would be unusable — it forbids documenting a config by writing about code. Measured against the real producer:

```
prose-first, `===` in the prose   → "== vdomRoot`, the wrapperStyle mechanism applies."   ← the defect
tag-first,   `===` still in prose → "{[isDescriptor]:true,merge:'shallow',value:null}"    ← correct
prose without `=`, tag after      → "{[isDescriptor]:true,merge:'shallow',value:null}"    ← correct
```

`indexOf('=')` takes the **first** `=` in the comment. So the hijack is not caused by an `=` existing in the prose — it is caused by an `=` existing **before the tag's own `=`**. Move the `@member` line above the prose and the same `===` is harmless.

**The accurate fourth property:**

> For an **Array or Object** member, the `@member` line must come **before** any prose containing `=`.

Two escapes, both value-preserving, which matters because the whole point of the §12 subsection is that no one should ever edit a default to satisfy the parser:

1. **Put the `@member` tag first** — keeps the prose exactly as written.
2. **Remove `=` from the prose** — "when vdom matches vdomRoot" instead of `` `vdom === vdomRoot` ``.

Neither touches the value. That is the property that distinguishes these from the unsupported-form table, where every option corrupts something.

**The cost of escape 1 is worth naming:** it inverts the conventional JSDoc order that §12 and the surrounding guidelines otherwise assume — description first, tags after. So the honest guideline is not "always put the tag first"; it is "**an Array/Object member whose description contains `=` must either lead with its tag or lose the `=`**", and an author should prefer the second unless the `=` is load-bearing.

`src/component/Base.mjs#style` is the case where it is load-bearing: the warning paragraph is *about* `vdom === vdomRoot` identity, and rewording it to avoid the operator would make the documentation worse to protect a parser. Leading with the tag is the right fix there.

Corpus figures from the earlier comment are unchanged — **144** members publishing a wrong default, **36** with descriptions polluted by the tail. What changes is only the shape of the rule that prevents new ones, and it is a much smaller ask than I first described. Still flagged rather than filed.
